title: SELECT
definition: To fetch certain columns in JQuery all you need is to write down the columns you need seperated by a ','

title: DISTINCT
definition:
Removes duplicate values from the result set.
The DISTINCT operation ensures that only unique values are returned for the selected column(s).
This is useful when you want to eliminate repeated data and retrieve only unique records.

title: GROUP BY
definition:
GROUP BY: A SQL clause that groups rows in a database table based on one or more columns, allowing for the aggregation of data (e.g., summing, counting, or averaging) within each group.
For example, if you have a sales database and want to find the total sales per region, you would use GROUP BY to group the sales data by region and then calculate the total for each group.

title: HAVING
definition: The HAVING clause was added to SQL because the WHERE keyword cannot be used with aggregate functions.

title: AS
definition: Aliases are used to give a table, or a column in a table, a temporary name.

title: LIMIT
definition: The LIMIT clause is to be used in an SQL query to specify the maximum number of results that one wishes to obtain. This clause is often associated with an OFFSET, that is to say to perform an offset on the result set. These 2 clauses allow for example to carry out pagination systems (example: retrieve the 10 articles of page 4).

title: OFFSET
definition:
Skips a specified number of rows before returning the query result.
The parameter defines how many rows should be ignored from the beginning of the result set.
This is commonly used for pagination together with LIMIT.

title: ORDER
definition: The ORDER BY command is used to sort the rows in a SQL query result. It is possible to sort the data on one or more columns, in ascending or descending order.

title: CASE...WHEN
definition:
Evaluates multiple conditions and returns a value depending on which condition is met.
The CASE expression works like an if-else structure in SQL. Each WHEN condition is evaluated in order, and the result of the first matching condition is returned.
If none of the conditions are satisfied, the ELSE value is returned.
This function is commonly used to categorize or transform values directly in a query.

Example use case: categorizing products based on their price (cheap, normal, expensive).
label: caseColumn

title: SUB QUERY
definition:
Allows using a query inside another query.
A subquery is executed first and its result is used by the main query.
This is useful for dynamic comparisons, such as filtering values based on aggregated results.
For example, you can retrieve products whose category starts with 'Con'

title: CTE
definition:
Defines a Common Table Expression (CTE), which creates a temporary named result set that can be referenced within the main query.
A CTE helps simplify complex queries by breaking them into reusable and readable parts.
This is useful for organizing subqueries, recursive queries, or intermediate calculations.
